title: 第2章 送画
content_zh:
如左晓瑶早能迅速从老者未尽的言语中知道他想表达的痛心一样，听到她又老借口重翻的想将此事含糊过去，老者颇有些怒其不争瞪着她道“这四幅画所表达出的意境，皆能令人心生感触，比你过去的那些为画而画的画强得多，不说身为画家，就说身为画者，也该是以创作为主，这是态度问题！”

“而你倒好，总拿那些死的图片做参考，然后成批的画，过去是为了你家经济条件，为了你奶奶的住院费用，我也就不说了，不仅不说，还帮你卖！现在你少了经济方面的压力，也确实能画出这样的好东西，怎么还像过去那样坚持你先前的想法呢！”

怕自己出声成了火上浇油，左晓瑶不敢打断，只好垂着脑袋任老者满心愤然心情讲完自己心中的愤慨。

“王爷爷，您先坐下，先别....别这火大啊，我过去画，是为钱，现在画，绝对是为爱好，这其中的想法当然有差别，而且差别大着呢，只是我觉得，我画画，只想为自己的需要，不想为那些虚名，什么画家不画家的，都无所谓....”

“我知道，您最遗憾的就是在我还没得到画家的名头前，为了点小钱，先毁了自个的前程，痛心被我浪费的好天赋，可我根本不在乎那些，当然也就不在乎你觉得我可能会得到、且该得的那些，我不承认自己有绘画天赋，不也是为了让您高兴点吗，您只要觉得我是烂泥扶不上墙的家伙，就不会老想着要把我拖出去现眼了呗！”

说到这个问题，左晓瑶觉得自己相当无辜，就跟老者很难理解她为什么毫不在乎自己的作品能不能出名，自己能不能得到更多人的认同和熟知一样，左晓瑶也很难理解人们为什么要那么在乎那些虚无飘渺的名声地位之类的东西，甚至为得到这些，还不惜千方百计的弄虚作假，违背良心道义，绞尽脑汁的设法炒作以博出名利。

人生在世，生命本就有限，只要能堂堂正正的尽量赚够生活所需，能简简单单的生活就好，何必让自己的一生活得那么复杂与疲惫。

而这一话题上，两人显然永远达不成一致意见，见到左晓瑶那讨好的笑容，老者心中的怒气顿时消去大半，她的画之所以让他颇为看重，在很大程度上，皆因画中所表达出那种平和与坚强，这是身为作者的她本身所具有的性格特质，所以能在不经意中通达她的画作表达出来，令其他人无法复制。

可这种特质，则恰恰是现代都市人身上所缺乏的，所以，在过去的多年里，即便她以自己最不屑的方式，拿在书上、网上或电视上相中的图片作参考，一幅接一幅的批量画同一图案，不留任何记号，销路倒还相当不错，有些老顾客甚至定期都会来指名要她的画。

虽明知道自个是气也白?遥??碜?揭巫由系睦险咴俅稳滩蛔〉闪怂?谎鄣馈八蛋桑?阏饣啬没?吹哪康模　?p>

即便从左晓瑶这回只拿过来四幅，且是四幅近期所画的非批量作品中看出她的目的与过去不同，但听到她的这个回答，老者还是颇有些不解。

“这几年，多亏有那么三四位老顾客一直捧场，我和奶奶的生活才有保障.....您别又生气，不管他们买画的目的是什么，反正我得了想要的钱就行，也多谢您一直帮我，所以这四幅就交给您，其中，这幅我最满意，是特意想送给您的，还请您不要拒绝才是！”

左晓瑶指着那幅画有夕阳洒满因有清风拂过而水波微荡的湖面的画强调道，与一般描写夕阳的画作常会表达出的日薄西山的迟暮遗憾之感不同，这幅画更多的则是突显夕阳的深沉与灿烂，光辉耀眼，异常夺目，令人因感叹大自然的神奇而心生向往之余，且还会在不自觉中隐怀着敬意。

许是她的劝慰起了效，老者这次没再情绪激动，只是叹了口气道“我知道你的心意，这世上，眼睁睁的看着别人拿自己的作品得名得利，还心怀感谢的，恐怕也就你这么个另类了吧！”

有那么两三个年青人仗着家里的势力，拿她卖出去的那些从不署名的画参加比赛，炒作成‘著名青年画家’，每每提起提起这事，都令尤为老者痛恨，次次皆火冒三丈。

毕竟这些画都是经过他的手流出，再加上他又总认为那些名利应属左晓瑶该有，却又时不时的见到那些人心安理得的顶着不属自己的名誉，总在电视、报纸、杂志上招摇过市，更令他郁闷得很。

而难得见老者这次没再发作，左晓瑶倒松了口气，笑着凑趣道“王爷爷真不愧是赶时髦的现代人，流行词张口就来啊！反正这些就麻烦您了，谁是想买去做什么的，您心里还是比较有数的，钱按老价格算，您看着卖吧，只是请您顺便跟他们说清楚，以后，我就不会像过去那样画了，也不会再随意拿出来卖，这个，算是我的心意！”

“这样就对了，放心，你会按的意思办好的，你奶奶在天上看着，也会安心些，这些年来，她嘴上不说，把你背着她不顾前程，拿老师和她最看重的东西换钱的事看在眼里，总觉得是她耽误了你，一直心存愧意！”

走出正信书画斋，为自己的卖画生涯画上一个句号，左晓瑶顺路在附近的服装市场逛了起来，自奶奶去后，她的穿衣风格也随之大变，不喜再穿那些五颜六色的色服，总是穿得非常素气，基本上皆是黑白色调，所以她衣柜里的那些过去的衣服却很少有这两种颜色，因奶奶觉得鲜艳的色彩会称得左晓瑶更有年轻人所特有的活力，会让她看着也跟着年轻不少。

这家市场里的衣服走的都是中低档路线，喊价都不低，但在高手面前，甚至能被砍去三分之二，左晓瑶没有与人磨嘴皮子的本事，所以从来都是对半砍，卖就买，不卖就走，即便走，大多时候都会被店家叫住，然后回身买下。

当然，这是在面对那些可买可不买的衣服时的情形，若是她真正相中的，作为从小到大，一向直接到根本懒得掩饰自己的她，即便店家不让步，只要在预算之内，基本上她也会买下，回去后再听籽佳笑话她又吃了多大的亏。

而这回本就是为买衣服而买，她更没有享受逛街选衣服的心情，基本上都是捡那些不带什么复杂图案、样式简单大方、黑色或白色的买，不接受半折砍价，就立马再换一家，仅花去大多逛街女孩只走过一两家店的时间，便已在花钱不多的情况下，满载而归。

回到家中，简单煮包方便面吃过之后，没心情上网，也没心思看电视，对着这套面积不足六十平方，被分成两室一厅的房子，左晓瑶再次拿出奶奶临终前甚重交待她要寻回，也就是留给她的这几样‘嫁妆’发呆，幻想着当初奶奶初次从众多聘礼里间第一眼相中它们的心情。

这三样东西明显是一套，皆是非金非银非铜非木的材质，样式极为古朴，应该年代已久，像是雕刻到上面的精致图案非常繁复，甚至还隐隐透着些神秘之感，但整体上给人的感觉却相当好，看走来十分漂亮。

如过去常用的模糊铜镜不同，这面巴掌大小的镜子能把人照得十分清晰，且是两面皆可照人，就那古代技术条件，这等做工可谓是相当高明，相较面言，这根头钗的样式倒相对普通许多，除上面的图案同样繁复外，没什么突出之处，看上去简单大方，是左晓瑶喜欢的风格。

略沉吟片刻后，她才又拿起嫁妆中的最后一样－篦之梳，这种两侧皆有齿的梳子，现代人极少用，但左晓瑶却相当熟悉，因为受奶奶的影响，从小到大，她常用的梳子基本都是这种款式的篦子梳。

她有一头很直很顺的长发，非常自然，从没做过任何烫、染、拉，从她还不记事开始，奶奶就一直很喜欢给她梳头，用的就是木制的这种篦子梳，梳齿较尖，而奶奶的动作却会很温柔，完全不会刺痛她的头皮，会将她的头发梳得非常散，然后再编成各式花样的发辫。

想到这些，哪怕明知道自己该恢复过去的坚强，眼泪却自有主有主张不停的往下流，失去至亲的悲伤与痛苦真的非常刻骨铭心，直到有切身体会时，左晓瑶才真正明白这种痛到底有多痛！

伤怀之时，手在无意中紧握住那篦子梳，即便手指因其中一侧较细的梳齿给刺到鲜血直流，心中痛到无以复加的左晓瑶也根本没注意到，反倒因手上传来的痛，缓解了些心中的悲伤。

当混着泪水的血沾到这三样东西上时，却被它们完全吸收的这诡异情景也未引起她的关注，而那三样东西则因吸收的血泪越来越多，竟逐渐泛出紫色光芒，它们本身的颜色也开始渐渐发生改变。

直到那光芒开始变得有些夺目时，笼罩住左晓瑶全身时，努力抬起头的她才发现情况有些不对，疑惑的低下头，却发现连她手中仍然紧握着的篦子梳在内，这三样东西竟已通体变成紫色，这一幕落在崇尚科学的现代人眼中，绝对算得上是相当诡异。

震惊之中，她下意识的松开手，只见那篦子梳、镜子与发钗竟随后便排成一行漂浮在她身前，这场景玄幻到令左晓瑶都有些怀疑自己是不是置身梦中，刚想抬手拉下头发试度痛不痛，与此同时，三样东西几乎是在同时突射出三道光芒完全将她罩住，令保持抬手姿势的她完全无法动弹，好在呼吸尚自如。

这种身体不受控制的时间好像并没持续太久，当瞪大双眼瞳空微缩的左晓瑶怔愣的看着那三样东西极为迅速的没入自己眉心处后，她的手总算垂了下来，只是接着她本人也晕了！
content_en:
Just as Zuo Xiaoyao could quickly understand the pain he wanted to express from the old man's unfinished words, when he heard her making excuses again to try to obscure the matter, the old man was quite angry and glared at her and said, "The artistic conception expressed in these four paintings can make people feel deeply. It is much better than the paintings you painted for the sake of painting in the past. Not only as a painter, but as a painter, you should focus on creation. This is a matter of attitude!"

"As for you, you always use those dead pictures as a reference, and then draw batches of them. In the past, it was for your family's financial conditions and for your grandma's hospitalization expenses. I won't say it. Not only did I not say it, but I also helped you sell it! Now that you are less under financial pressure and can indeed draw such good things, why do you still insist on your previous ideas like in the past!"

Afraid that speaking out would add fuel to the fire, Zuo Xiaoyao did not dare to interrupt, so she had no choice but to lower her head and let the old man finish his indignation with a heart full of anger.

"Grandpa Wang, please sit down first, and don't be so angry. I used to paint for money, but now I paint for love. Of course, there are differences in my thoughts, and the differences are huge. But I feel that I only paint for my own needs, not for those who have false reputations. It doesn't matter whether I am a painter or not..."

"I know that your biggest regret is that before I got the name of a painter, you ruined your own career for a little money, and feel sad that I wasted my good talent. But I don't care about those at all, and of course I don't care about what you think I might get and deserve. I don't admit that I have painting talent, isn't it just to make you happy? As long as you think that I am a guy who can't support the wall, you won't always think about dragging me out to show off!"

When it comes to this issue, Zuo Xiaoyao feels that she is quite innocent. Just as it is difficult for the old man to understand why she does not care whether her works can be famous or not, and whether she can be recognized and known by more people, it is also difficult for Zuo Xiaoyao to understand why people care so much about things like illusory reputation and status, and even go to great lengths to deceive and violate their conscience and morality to gain fame and fortune.

Life is limited in this world. As long as you can earn as much as you can for your living needs and live a simple life, there is no need to make your life so complicated and tiring.

On this topic, it was obvious that the two would never reach an agreement. Seeing Zuo Xiaoyao's flattering smile, most of the anger in the old man's heart disappeared immediately. The reason why he valued her paintings was, to a large extent, because of the peace and strength expressed in them. This was her own character trait as an author, so she could inadvertently express it in her paintings, making it impossible for others to copy.

But this quality is precisely what modern urbanites lack. Therefore, in the past many years, even though she used the most disdainful way, using the pictures in books, online or on TV as reference, she painted the same pattern in batches one after another without leaving any marks. The sales were quite good, and some old customers even came to request her paintings regularly.

Even though I know I am angry, it is useless. I am far away.

Even though Zuo Xiaoyao only took four pieces this time, and they were four recently painted non-batch works, it could be seen that her purpose was different from the past, but the old man was still a little puzzled when he heard her answer.

"In the past few years, thanks to the support of three or four old customers, my grandma and I have a secure life... Don't be angry again. No matter what their purpose of buying paintings is, I just have to get the money I want. Thank you for always helping me, so I will give these four paintings to you. Among them, I am most satisfied with this one. I specially wanted to give it to you. Please don't refuse!"

Zuo Xiaoyao pointed to the painting of the setting sun filling the lake with swaying waves due to the breeze, and stressed that unlike the general paintings depicting the setting sun that often express the regret of the sunset, this painting highlights the depth and brilliance of the setting sun.

Maybe her persuasion had an effect. The old man didn't get emotional anymore this time. He just sighed and said, "I know what you mean. In this world, I'm afraid you are the only one who can watch other people gain fame and benefit from their works while still being grateful!"

There were two or three young people who relied on their family's power to participate in competitions with the unsigned paintings she sold and hyped them up as 'famous young painters'. Every time this was mentioned, the old man especially hated him and became furious every time.

After all, these paintings came out through his hands, and he always believed that the fame and fortune should belong to Zuo Xiaoyao, but from time to time he saw people who were content with reputations that were not their own, always showing off on TV, newspapers, and magazines, which made him even more depressed.

It was rare to see that the old man didn't have another attack this time. Zuo Xiaoyao breathed a sigh of relief and joked with a smile, "Grandpa Wang is indeed a modern person who follows the fashion. He comes up with buzzwords as soon as he opens his mouth! Anyway, these are troublesome for you. Who wants to buy something? YouI still know better. The money is based on the old price. You can sell it. I just ask you to make it clear to them. In the future, I will not paint it like I did in the past, and I will not sell it casually. This is my intention!"

"That's right. Don't worry, you will do it as you want. Your grandma is watching from the sky, and she will feel at ease. Over the years, she has not said anything, but she has seen that you went behind her back and ignored your future, exchanging the teacher and her most valued things for money. I always feel that she has delayed you, and I have always felt guilty!"

After walking out of the Zhengxin Painting and Calligraphy Studio and putting an end to her painting-selling career, Zuo Xiaoyao stopped by and strolled around the nearby clothing market. After her grandma left, her dressing style also changed drastically. She no longer liked wearing those colorful clothes and always dressed very inappropriately.Chang Suqi is basically in black and white, so the old clothes in her wardrobe rarely have these two colors, because grandma feels that bright colors will make Zuo Xiaoyao more energetic and unique to young people, and will make her look much younger.

The clothes in this market are all medium and low-end, and the bidding prices are not low, but in front of experts, they can even be cut off by two-thirds. Zuo Xiaoyao has no ability to talk to others, so she always cuts them in half, buys when they are sold, and leaves when they are not sold. Even if she leaves, most of the time she will be stopped by the store, and then she turns around and buys.

Of course, this is the situation when faced with clothes that can be bought or not. If she really likes the clothes, she has always been direct and doesn't bother to hide herself since she was a child. Even if the store doesn't give in, as long as it is within the budget, she will basically buy it. After returning home, she will suffer a big loss when listening to Zijia's jokes.

This time, she was buying clothes for the purpose, and she didn't enjoy shopping and choosing clothes. She basically bought those without complicated patterns, simple and elegant styles, black or white. If she didn't accept half-off bargains, she would immediately change to another store. It only took the time of most shopping girls to walk through one or two stores, and she returned with a full load without spending much money.

After returning home and eating some instant noodles, she was not in the mood to surf the Internet or watch TV. Facing this house with an area of ​​less than 60 square meters and divided into two bedrooms and one living room, Zuo Xiaoyao once again took out the "dowry" her grandma had left her to find, which was what her grandma had told her before she died, and she was in a daze, imagining how her grandma felt when she first saw them among the many betrothal gifts.

These three things are obviously a set. They are all made of materials that are neither gold, silver, copper, nor wood. Their styles are extremely simple and must have been around for a long time. The exquisite patterns carved on them are very complicated and even have a vague sense of mystery. However, the overall feeling is quite good and they look very beautiful.

Unlike the fuzzy bronze mirrors commonly used in the past, this palm-sized mirror can illuminate people very clearly, and it can illuminate people from both sides. Considering the ancient technical conditions, the workmanship can be said to be quite superb. Compared with the surface, the style of this hairpin is relatively ordinary. Except for the same complicated pattern on it, there is nothing outstanding. It looks simple and elegant, which is Zuo Xiaoyao's favorite style.

After pondering for a moment, she picked up the last item in her dowry - the grate comb. This kind of comb with teeth on both sides is rarely used by modern people, but Zuo Xiaoyao is very familiar with it. Because of her grandmother's influence, the combs she commonly used since childhood were basically this style of grate comb.

She has very straight and smooth long hair, which is very natural and has never been permed, dyed or pulled. Ever since she can remember, her grandma has always liked to comb her hair. She uses a wooden comb with sharp teeth, but her movements are very gentle and will not hurt her scalp at all. She will comb her hair very loosely and then braid it into various patterns.

Thinking of this, even though she knew that she should regain her past strength, tears kept flowing down of her own accord. The sadness and pain of losing a loved one was really unforgettable. It was not until she experienced it personally that Zuo Xiaoyao truly understood how painful this pain was!

When she was feeling sad, her hand inadvertently held the grate comb tightly. Even though her fingers were pricked by the thin comb teeth on one side, blood flowed, and Zuo Xiaoyao, who was in so much pain, didn't notice it at all. Instead, the pain in her hand relieved some of the sadness in her heart.

When the blood mixed with tears touched these three things, the strange sight of being completely absorbed by them did not attract her attention. As the three things absorbed more and more blood and tears, they gradually glowed purple, and their own colors began to gradually change.

It wasn't until the light began to become a bit dazzling and enveloped Zuo Xiaoyao's whole body that she tried to raise her head and realized that something was wrong. She lowered her head in confusion, only to find that even the comb she was still holding tightly in her hand, these three things had turned purple. This scene was definitely quite weird in the eyes of modern people who advocate science.

In shock, she subconsciously let go of her hand, only to see the comb, mirror and hairpin floating in a row in front of her. The scene was so fantastical that Zuo Xiaoyao even doubted whether she was in a dream. She was about to raise her hand and pull down her hair to see if it hurt. At the same time, three things shot out three rays of light almost at the same time and completely covered her, making her unable to move at all while keeping her hand raised. Fortunately, she could still breathe freely.

The time when her body was out of control didn't seem to last long. When Zuo Xiaoyao, whose eyes were wide open and her eyes were narrowed, stared blankly at the three things that quickly sank into her eyebrows, her hands finally dropped down, but then she herself fainted!
